text:
The defendant's conscious disregard of a substantial and unjustifiable risk by speeding on a busy street, combined with his admitted indifference to the consequences, supports a finding of recklessness rather than intent. Between the given options, battery is the better fit because the pedestrian was actually struck and seriously injured, whereas attempted manslaughter requires an intent to kill that is absent here. Thus he should be found guilty of battery.

CONFIDENCE: 70
